headline: Britain stopped working for nine days in May, Goddard flew a liquid-fuel rocket, and Valentino died at thirty-one
texture: The British general strike began at midnight on May 4 in support of the miners and was called off by the unions before the miners themselves gave in. Robert Goddard launched the first liquid-fuel rocket at Auburn, Massachusetts on March 16, and it went up about as far as a house. Richard Byrd and Floyd Bennett claimed a flight over the North Pole in May, a claim argued over ever since.

Warner Brothers put its Vitaphone system in front of a New York audience on August 5 with Don Juan, which carried a synchronised orchestral score and no talking at all. It finished fifth for the year with $1,258,000 in rentals, behind What Price Glory? and Douglas Fairbanks in The Black Pirate. Rudolph Valentino died on August 23 at thirty-one and the crowds outside the funeral home in New York turned into a riot.

The NBC Radio Network opened in November with twenty-four stations, the first permanent national network in the United States. John Logie Baird demonstrated his mechanical television in January to an audience that had no reason to care yet. A. A. Milne published Winnie-the-Pooh in London on October 14. Claude Monet died on December 5 and Rainer Maria Rilke on December 29.

notes: Research pass July 2026. No prices section: the three price series all start later. Harry Houdini died this year on a date the source would not yield cleanly, so he is left out rather than dated from memory. Hirohito's accession carries no date for the same reason: the source line merges it with an unrelated event. The rocket going up about as far as a house, and the crowd at Valentino's funeral becoming a riot, are general knowledge of those subjects rather than claims from the year pages.
